Large-scale events require Sicherheitskonzept (safety concept) under §30 ThürBauO, fire safety certification, and medical standby. Events on public premises require Gestattung under GastG. The festival generates €30M+ annual economic impact for Erfurt. Monument protection (ThürDSchG) limits technical infrastructure anchoring on the cathedral steps.
laws.penalty: Event without required Gestattung: GastG §28 fines up to €5,000; crowd safety violations: immediate event shutdown by Ordnungsamt; §315 StGB endangering public traffic near mass events
exceptions: Religious church services at Dom exempt from secular VersG/GastG event permit requirements under Art. 140 GG / Art. 137 WRV Kirchenrecht

quiz.q: What is the maximum spectator capacity per performance at the Domstufenfestspiele Erfurt?
quiz.explanation: The Domstufenfestspiele Erfurt accommodates up to approximately 25,000 spectators per performance at the Cathedral Steps, making it Germany's largest open-air opera festival, subject to comprehensive VersG and safety regulation.

laws.title: FSU Jena 1558 – ThürHSChG & Hochschulrecht
laws.subtitle: University law, foundation funding and Thuringia's academic landscape
laws.fullDescription: The Thüringer Hochschulgesetz (ThürHSChG) governs Thuringia's 12 universities and Fachhochschulen. FSU Jena (Friedrich-Schiller-Universität, 1558) has 20,000 students; TU Ilmenau specializes in engineering and technology; Erfurt University is Germany's only university refounded under canon law tradition. Under HRG (Hochschulrahmengesetz) and ThürHSChG, universities have Lehrfreiheit (academic freedom). The Ernst Abbe Stiftung supports science education in Jena. Thuringia spends €700M annually on higher education; 60,000 students total.
laws.penalty: Academic fraud (Täuschung in Prüfungen): Exmatrikulation (expulsion) under ThürHSChG §23; plagiarism leading to fraudulent doctorate: §263 StGB title fraud
exceptions: Private Hochschulen accredited by Akkreditierungsrat but not state-funded are not subject to full ThürHSChG public governance provisions

quiz.q: In which year was the Friedrich-Schiller-Universität Jena (FSU) founded?
quiz.explanation: The Friedrich-Schiller-Universität Jena (FSU) was founded in 1558 under Duke Johann Friedrich II of Saxony. Today it has approximately 20,000 students and is Thuringia's flagship research university.

laws.title: Thüringer Rostbratwurst PGI & Saale-Unstrut WeinG
laws.subtitle: Geographical indication law and Thuringia's culinary heritage
laws.fullDescription: Thuringia has multiple EU-protected food products: Thüringer Rostbratwurst (PGI since 2004), Thüringer Leberwurst (PGI), and Thüringer Rotwurst (PGI). The Thüringer Klöße (potato dumplings) are a regional specialty but lack formal GI protection. Under UWG (Gesetz gegen unlauteren Wettbewerb) §5, misleading geographical origin claims are prohibited. EU Regulation 1151/2012 governs PDO/PGI registrations; applications by regional producer associations. Thuringia's Saale-Unstrut wine region (700 ha, Germany's northernmost) has Qualitätswein status under WeinG.
laws.penalty: False PGI origin labeling: UWG §5 injunction and damages; EU Regulation 1151/2012 violation: fines up to €500,000 at member state discretion
exceptions: Generic terms such as Bratwurst or Leberwurst without regional modifier are not protected; only the full designation 'Thüringer Rostbratwurst' carries PGI protection

quiz.q: Since what year has the Thüringer Rostbratwurst been protected as an EU Protected Geographical Indication (PGI)?
quiz.explanation: The Thüringer Rostbratwurst received EU PGI status in 2004, protecting its distinctive recipe — primarily pork seasoned with marjoram and caraway — from imitation by non-Thuringian producers.

laws.title: WISMUT Sanierung Ronneburg – AtG & Umwelthaftungsrecht
laws.subtitle: Federal uranium mining cleanup law and environmental liability
laws.fullDescription: WISMUT GmbH, jointly owned by the Federal Republic (100%), has spent €6.4bn cleaning up uranium mining contamination across Thuringia (Ronneburg) and Saxony (Aue, Schlema). Under AtG (Atomgesetz) and WISMUT-Bereinigungsgesetz 1991, the federal government assumed full liability for all environmental damage. Ronneburg's waste pile (Haldenkomplex Lichtenberg) — the world's largest uranium tailings pile at 130 million tonnes — was remediated for the 2007 Federal Garden Show (Bundesgartenschau). Groundwater monitoring continues until 2045.
laws.penalty: AtG §46: nuclear facility operator strict liability (Gefährdungshaftung) without proof of fault; unlimited liability for nuclear damage
exceptions: WISMUT GmbH government ownership means §839 BGB state liability applies; private contractors on WISMUT sites covered by WISMUT GmbH indemnity agreements

quiz.q: How much has the federal government spent on WISMUT uranium mining cleanup in Thuringia and Saxony?
quiz.explanation: WISMUT GmbH, 100% federally owned, has spent approximately €6.4 billion on uranium mining remediation across its former operations in Thuringia (Ronneburg) and Saxony, with groundwater monitoring continuing until 2045.

laws.title: ThürKO – Kommunalordnung & Gebietsreform 6 Kreisfreie Städte
laws.subtitle: Municipal law and Thuringia's territorial reform
laws.fullDescription: The Thüringer Kommunalordnung (ThürKO) governs Thuringia's 17 Landkreise, 6 kreisfreie Städte (Erfurt, Jena, Gera, Weimar, Suhl, Eisenach), and approximately 700 municipalities (Gemeinden) following the 2019–2021 voluntary merger reform. Pre-reform Thuringia had 840+ municipalities, many with fewer than 200 inhabitants. ThürKO allows Gemeinschaftsverwaltungen (shared administrations) for small municipalities. The Bürgermeister (directly elected) and Gemeinderat (council) form the dual executive-representative structure. ThürKO §36 mandates balanced Gemeinde budgets; persistent deficit leads to Haushaltssicherungskonzept.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized Gemeinde spending beyond budget: ThürKO §70 Landratsamt intervention; Bürgermeister financial misconduct: §266 StGB Untreue (breach of trust)
exceptions: Zweckverbände (special-purpose associations) formed between municipalities for joint services (water, waste) governed separately under ThürKGG rather than ThürKO

quiz.q: How many kreisfreie Städte (independent cities) does Thuringia have under the ThürKO?
quiz.explanation: Thuringia has 6 kreisfreie Städte not belonging to a Landkreis: Erfurt, Jena, Gera, Weimar, Suhl, and Eisenach, each governed directly under the ThürKO with full municipal and Landkreis-level administrative competencies.

laws.title: JENOPTIK AG – AWG & Dual-Use Exportkontrolle
laws.subtitle: Jena precision optics company and arms export control law
laws.fullDescription: JENOPTIK AG (Jena, SDAX-listed) employs 4,400 globally in photonics, sensors, and smart transportation systems. Spun off from Carl-Zeiss-Stiftung 1991 via Treuhand restructuring; the state of Thuringia sold its last stake in 2004. JENOPTIK's defense division (optics for Leopard tanks, missiles) requires BAFA (Bundesamt für Wirtschaft und Ausfuhrkontrolle) export licenses under AWG (Außenwirtschaftsgesetz) and AVV (Außenwirtschaftsverordnung). EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821 governs civilian-military dual-use optics. JENOPTIK annual revenue: €1.1bn (2023).
laws.penalty: Unauthorized dual-use export: AWG §17 up to 5 years imprisonment and unlimited fine; BAFA license violation: immediate business suspension
exceptions: Intra-EU transfers of dual-use goods under EU Regulation 2021/821 simplified to general export authorization (GEA) for low-risk items between EU member states

quiz.q: Which federal authority issues export licenses for JENOPTIK's dual-use defense optics under German export control law?
quiz.explanation: BAFA (Bundesamt für Wirtschaft und Ausfuhrkontrolle) is the federal authority responsible for issuing export licenses for dual-use goods and military equipment under AWG and AVV, including JENOPTIK's defense optics destined for military applications abroad.

laws.title: ILB/IFB Thüringen – ThürAufbauBankG & Wirtschaftsförderung
laws.subtitle: State development bank law and investment promotion in Thuringia
laws.fullDescription: The Thüringer Aufbaubank (TAB) is Thuringia's state development bank (Förderbank), established under ThürAufbauBankG, providing subsidized loans (Förderkredite), guarantees, and EU structural fund (EFRE, ESF) distribution. TAB manages €3bn+ in loan commitments supporting SME investment, housing construction, and renewable energy. In 2024, TAB administered €400M in EFRE funds under the Thuringia REACT-EU program. Beneficiary eligibility and grant conditions are binding under public subsidy law (Subventionsrecht); misuse leads to full repayment under §49a VwVfG.
laws.penalty: Subsidy fraud (Subventionsbetrug): §264 StGB up to 5 years; incorrect TAB grant applications: €49a VwVfG full repayment plus interest at 3% above base rate
exceptions: De minimis aid under EU Regulation 1407/2013 (up to €300,000 per 3 years) exempt from full state aid notification requirements to EU Commission

quiz.q: What is the EU de minimis aid threshold that exempts state grants from full EU Commission notification requirements?
quiz.explanation: Under EU Regulation 1407/2013, state aid of up to €300,000 per 3-year period per enterprise qualifies as de minimis aid, exempt from the standard EU state aid notification and approval procedure applicable to larger grants.

laws.title: Thüringer Datenschutzgesetz – TLfDI & DSGVO-Vollzug
laws.subtitle: State data protection law and Thuringia's data protection authority
laws.fullDescription: The Thüringer Datenschutzgesetz (ThürDSG) supplements DSGVO (EU GDPR) for public sector bodies; the TLfDI (Thüringer Landesbeauftragter für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit) is the independent supervisory authority under Art. 51 DSGVO. TLfDI supervises all Thuringia state agencies, municipalities, and public companies. Private sector GDPR enforcement falls to TLfDI under §40 BDSG allocation. ThürIFG (Thüringer Informationsfreiheitsgesetz) grants public access to government information within 1 month; exemptions for ongoing investigations and personal data. The AfD-led government's 2024 data retention proposals were reviewed by TLfDI for DSGVO compatibility.
laws.penalty: DSGVO Art. 83(4): administrative fines up to €10M or 2% global turnover for processor violations; Art. 83(5): up to €20M or 4% global turnover for core principle violations
exceptions: Journalistic privilege under §9c BDSG and ThürDSG allows media processing personal data without full DSGVO compliance for editorial purposes

quiz.q: What is the maximum GDPR fine for core principle violations under Art. 83(5) DSGVO?
quiz.explanation: DSGVO Art. 83(5) sets the maximum administrative fine at €20 million or 4% of total worldwide annual turnover (whichever is higher) for violations of core principles such as lawfulness of processing, data subject rights, and international transfer rules.
